text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementEnvironmentElephants Engineer Their Ecosystems Even in DeathIt’s the circle of lifeJCBy Jake Currie4:00 PM CDT on October 13, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleElephants are ecosystem engineers. They trample trees, loosen soil with their tusks, and can even create trails and watering holes. According to a new study published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, these massive beasts continue to sculpt the savannas long after their deaths. To investigate the impact of elephant carcasses on the ecosystems, biologists from the University of California, Santa Barbara spent nearly eight years sampling the soil and plant life from 40 different carcass sites scattered throughout South Africa’s Kruger National Park. Read more: “Is Poaching Causing Elephants to Evolve Without Tusks?”Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
